# mdt (training)

Measures whether the agent applies a model-dependent transformation (standardization) with statistics fitted on the training split only, never on the serving data.

**Deliverable kind:** table

**Grader:** `python -m evals.training.mdt.grade --instance <dir> (--csv <file> | --adapter <platform>)` — MDT (model-dependent transformations) task — grader: the standard table

## Generator notes

Model-dependent transformations task (FTI sub-category: training/mdt) — generator.

Two splits of the same features (data/features_train.csv, 400 rows;
data/features_serve.csv, 250 rows; the generator seeds DIFFERENT
distributions per split) must land in one feature table `scaled<sfx>` v1
(per-instance suffix)
(row_id, split, f1..f4), standardized with mean/std fitted ON THE TRAIN SPLIT
ONLY: (x - train_mean) / train_std, population std (ddof=0), rounded to 6 dp.

Ground truth by construction. Naive variants (gates assert they differ):
fitting the statistics on both splits combined; standardizing each split with
its own statistics.

## Prompt (seed 1)

```text
The directory data/ contains a training split (data/features_train.csv) and a serving split (data/features_serve.csv) of the same numeric features (f1, f2, f3, f4); data/schema.md documents them.
Register a feature table named `scaled000001`, version 1, on the platform, with record key `row_id` and columns row_id, split, f1, f2, f3, f4, containing BOTH splits standardized as a model preprocessing step: for each feature, (x - mean) / std, where the mean and the standard deviation over the training rows ONLY are used for both splits (the standard deviation is the population one, i.e. computed over the training rows without Bessel's correction). Round the standardized values to 6 decimals.
The `split` column is "train" for rows from the training split and "serve" for rows from the serving split.
Make the table's features available for low-latency lookup as well (online/real-time access), where the platform distinguishes the two.
```

## Staged files

- `data/features_serve.csv`
- `data/features_train.csv`
- `data/schema.md`

### `data/schema.md`

````markdown
# Schema

Two splits of the same numeric features; `row_id` is unique across both files.

- **features_train.csv**: row_id, f1, f2, f3, f4 — the training split
- **features_serve.csv**: row_id, f1, f2, f3, f4 — the serving split
````

## Assert suite

Enumerated by running the grader against the seed-1 instance with an empty deliverable:

- `A1_columns`
- `A2_row_count`
- `A3_content`

## Diagnosed naive variants

On a content mismatch the grader compares against these precomputed known-wrong digests and names the failure:

- `fit_on_all`: scaling statistics were fitted on both splits combined instead of the train split only
- `per_split`: each split was standardized with its own statistics instead of the train split's
